title: mu-law encode and decode
goal:
WaveNet compands each sample with $f(x) = \operatorname{sign}(x)\,\ln(1+\mu|x|)/\ln(1+\mu)$ for $-1 < x < 1$ and $\mu = 255$, then quantizes to 256 values (Section 2.2). Write:

- `mu_law_encode(x, mu=255)` takes floats in $[-1, 1]$ and returns integers in $0 \dots \mu$. Compute $f(x)$, then map $[-1, 1]$ to $[0, \mu]$ and round to the nearest integer.
- `mu_law_decode(q, mu=255)` takes integers in $0 \dots \mu$ and returns floats, using the exact inverse $x = \operatorname{sign}(f)\,((1+\mu)^{|f|} - 1)/\mu$.

The paper doesn't say how to index the 256 bins. This exercise uses `q = floor((f + 1) / 2 * mu + 0.5)`, the convention in common WaveNet code.
hints: `np.log1p(a)` computes `log(1 + a)` accurately for small `a`. `np.expm1` is its inverse.
Map $f \in [-1, 1]$ to $[0, \mu]$ with `(f + 1) / 2 * mu`, and round with `np.floor(... + 0.5)`.
Decode first maps `q` back to `f = 2 * q / mu - 1`, and then applies the inverse of the compression. Keep `np.sign(f)` and use `np.abs(f)` inside the power.
